content: The use of local wound analgesia is a technique employed to manage pain in infants undergoing thoracic or abdominal surgical procedures. This approach involves the administration of analgesic agents directly into the wound site to provide targeted pain relief. It is particularly beneficial in this population due to the challenges associated with systemic analgesics, such as opioids, which can lead to significant side effects in neonates and infants. Local wound analgesia minimizes systemic drug exposure while effectively controlling postoperative pain. This method is often integrated into multimodal pain management strategies to enhance recovery and reduce the risk of complications associated with inadequate pain control in this vulnerable age group.
